title: Chromasmith UI/UX design backlog
source_scope: Recommendations 1-70 from the two supplied review documents; recommendations 71-100 from the follow-up review in this task.

priority_guide.P0: Urgent trust/usability defect or enabling gate

model_guide.codex:gpt-6-astra: Best default for difficult end-to-end repository changes, broad state coverage, architecture, or research-heavy implementation.
model_guide.codex:gpt-5.6-terra: Best default for bounded implementation in this repository where deterministic tests and focused edits dominate.
model_guide.claude-code:claude-opus-5: Recommended when visual judgement, screenshot comparison, or interaction design is the main challenge; pair with repo tests and human visual review.
model_guide.claude-code:claude-sonnet-5: Recommended for smaller, well-scoped UI changes and routine implementation; promote to a stronger model if scope or ambiguity grows.

observed_findings.summary: Review screenshots showed a Library count of 57,651 while All Photos displayed no photos and the footer showed 0 of 0; the Working status appeared unchanged after clicks.
observed_findings.disposition: Keep as a diagnostic finding, not one of the 100 numbered design recommendations. Investigate/reproduce before implementation; item 16 covers user-facing state design.
observed_findings.completion_evidence: 2026-09-14: reproduced the empty-root launch and stale smart-collection paths. Library now restores a versioned destination (folder, collection, catalog/date scope, or Lightroom album); stale registry/history paths are excluded from sidebar and footer totals while preserved for recovery. Focused lib:test checks passed for saved collection/date restoration and 8 visible Edited photos matching sidebar/footer 8 of 8.

items.title: Show selection actions only when they can act
items.acceptance: No-photo state has no active destructive or export actions; selection state exposes the correct actions and counts.
items.completion_evidence: desktop/library-ui.js: added syncLibActionButtons() (near syncLibFlagRow, ~L6508) that disables #lib-flag-reject/#lib-flag-fav/#lib-flag-pick when no photo is open (state.openedPath empty) and #lib-export-btn/#lib-allfx-btn when nothing can act (cmKbTargets() empty: no selection, no keyboard cursor, no open photo); wired into renderGridTail, updateCardSelClasses, openEditInHandoff and the flag-button click handlers so it tracks selection/open-photo changes. Added .lib-btn:disabled CSS (opacity .4, no pointer events) using only existing --sur2/--bdr/--txt tokens, no new values. The pre-existing lib-batchbar (>=2 selected) already showed correct counts/actions and was left unchanged. Verified live via desktop/dist build served from a staged /tmp copy (?libtest=1): fresh load / nothing selected -> all five buttons disabled; single click selects (no open) -> Export/All FX enable, flag row stays disabled (rates the open photo only, unchanged prior behavior); second click opens the photo -> flag row also enables. npm run ui:test shows the same pre-existing unrelated failures (export@ TAP, looks@ CONTRAST) with and without this change — no new regressions.

items.title: Design friendly Library loading, empty, and error states
items.acceptance: No raw developer error reaches users; loading, genuinely empty, and recoverable error states each offer a clear next action.

items.title: Center the Library empty state around one primary action
items.acceptance: At supported widths, the primary import action is centered, secondary action is subordinate, and labels never wrap awkwardly.

items.title: Reduce visual clutter from unavailable actions
items.acceptance: Unavailable controls remain discoverable when needed, explain their prerequisite, and do not compete with available actions.
items.implementation_note: Library toolbar actions require an explicit Library selection and target that selection; the Editor's own controls continue to target its edited photo. A visible prerequisite hint is shown only when selection is empty. Automated test currently confirms the no-selection state, but selected-card targeting still needs a reliable browser regression check before closure.
items.validation_evidence: 2026-09-14: desktop build succeeds. Focused Playwright run confirmed all five controls are disabled with the hint visible and aria-described; later selection assertions could not reliably observe the harness card selection and were removed rather than treated as proof. Item remains in_progress pending a reliable selected-batch interaction check and visual capture.

items.title: Make progress notices resolve into completion or failure
items.acceptance: Progress updates advance and resolve; completion and failure are announced accessibly and do not remain stale.
items.completion_evidence: Added a pinned toastProgress(msg) API to chromasmith-22.html's toast engine that stays open with a pulsing indicator until update()/resolve()/fail() is called, instead of the old fire-and-forget toast() timing out on a fixed 1.9s/3.4s clock regardless of whether the underlying operation was still running. Added role=status/aria-live=polite/aria-atomic to the shared toast element so completion and failure are announced to assistive tech, not just shown visually. In desktop/library-ui.js, converted the collage build, HDR merge, focus stack, astro stack, panorama stitch, and recursive subfolder-scan progress toasts (previously separate toast() calls that could go stale mid-op) to toastProgress(), each resolving to a completion or failure message when its invoke() settles. Verified with node test/export_harness.mjs (30/30 renders, no GLSL compile errors) and npm run ui:test — the remaining ui_audit failures (TAP/CONTRAST/PARITY-MISSING) are pre-existing and unrelated, confirmed identical with the change stashed out.
items.notes: Scoped to explicit start/end progress toasts (collage/HDR/focus/astro/pano merges, subfolder scan). Left selectAllCatalogEntries()'s "Loading all N photos…" toast alone — it has no matching failure/success pair today and adding one was out of scope for this item.

items.title: Show per-photo progress for decode and analysis work
items.acceptance: Every photo-specific decode or analysis operation shows a local, understandable loading status for that photo and clears on success or failure.
items.notes: Scope confirmed by user: anything that results in loading is in scope. Implemented photo/video decode and RAW re-decode status, RAW denoise, AI Select encode/refine, depth estimation, face parsing, Library thumbnail decode, and per-photo faces/pets/face-embedding/CLIP indexing badges. Library scan events now carry the affected photo paths for those four analysis stages; the Editor status has a local overlay when the deskbar title is unavailable. Checks: Library photo-activity Playwright test passed in dark and light themes; focused Editor lifecycle test passed once before the narrow-layout fallback was added, but later attempts timed out during initial page navigation; CDP diagnostic confirmed the narrow-layout status call settles without a hang. `git diff --check`, Editor fast structural checks, and Rust `cargo check` passed. Keep in progress: full visual screenshot inspection and a clean focused Editor lifecycle run remain outstanding; audit any additional photo-specific catalog stages before closure.

items.title: Add a persistent activity centre for long operations
items.acceptance: Import, index, cache and export activity survives navigation and exposes safe pause/cancel actions where supported.
items.notes: 2026-09-14: fixed a stuck-forever bug in the pill (desktop/library-ui.js's `#lib-activity`, already built as the merge of catalog-scan/import/job-progress events) reported as 'stuck on working'. Root cause: merge_hdr_photos/merge_focus_photos/merge_astro_photos/merge_panorama_photos (desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs) only called emit_job(...,"done",...) on their success path, after `?` had every chance to return early on a decode/align/blend error — so a failed merge left the pill parked on whatever phase it was last at ('align'/'blend') forever, and since these jobs carry no cancelFn there was no Cancel action to clear it either (clicking it, once the 90s stall watchdog showed the button, only closed the popover). Fix: (1) each merge command now runs its work inside an `async` block and emits "done" unconditionally afterward, on both success and failure; (2) library-ui.js's Cancel button now falls back to dismissing the pill for any non-catalog job with no real cancelFn, so a wedged pill can never get permanently stuck regardless of backend behavior. Could not run `cargo check`/the JS test suite/a live app session — this Windows checkout has no Rust or Node toolchain installed; validated by manual code review only (diff is minimal and structurally mirrors the pre-existing capture pattern). Scope: only the stuck-pill bug, not the rest of item 7's acceptance criteria (export activity, full pause/cancel coverage) — status left as-is.

items.title: Make Export summarize and open the active queue
items.acceptance: Queued exports show progress and destination; failures and completed outputs remain inspectable.

items.title: Replace black thumbnail tiles with photo-derived placeholders
items.acceptance: Real library loading never presents a misleading solid-black tile; placeholder transitions to image without layout shift.

items.title: Show collection counts consistently
items.acceptance: Counts appear consistently, remain secondary in hierarchy, and match the displayed collection.

items.title: Dim inactive sidebar labels, icons and counts
items.acceptance: Inactive navigation recedes while the active row remains clear; contrast stays readable.
items.completion_evidence: desktop/library-ui.js: inactive .lib-coll-row labels and inherited icons use the existing --ink-muted-80 token, mapped to --ink-on-dark-muted in dark mode and #333 in light mode; selected rows retain their existing high-contrast accent/ink rules. The existing muted count treatment remains unchanged. In the staged Library at 1440×900, dark inactive navigation measured 8.92:1 contrast; light inactive labels measured 11.60:1 and the selected row retained semibold Blue Slate text/icons/count. lint:library-content, tokens:check, tokens:verify, and git diff --check pass. The wireframe inventory hover finding and four responsive topbar/640px layout findings are explicitly waived by the user on 2026-09-14 for this navigation-only commit.

items.title: Shorten and clarify Library search wording
items.acceptance: Placeholder fits narrow supported widths and describes the searchable content without truncation.

items.title: Group Library toolbar controls by purpose
items.acceptance: View, filter and action groups are visually distinct, keyboard reachable, and responsive without clipping.

items.title: Move maintenance commands out of collection browsing
items.acceptance: Verify, cleanup and maintenance actions are reachable in a clearly named utility location and no longer interrupt browsing.

items.title: Offer an aspect-aware justified gallery layout
items.acceptance: A layout option respects image aspect ratios, preserves stable scanning and supports keyboard selection.

items.title: Collapse the Library sidebar to an icon rail at narrow widths
items.acceptance: No labels clip at tested widths; collapsed controls retain accessible names and predictable expansion.

items.title: Add a keyboard-first culling view
items.acceptance: Single-photo preview, neighbouring filmstrip and configurable pick/reject/navigation shortcuts work together.

items.title: Add a keyboard command menu for global navigation and actions
items.acceptance: Keyboard search finds available photos, tools and actions; commands respect current context and disabled prerequisites.

items.title: Add consistent single-key view shortcuts and a shortcut guide
items.acceptance: Shortcuts are documented in-app, avoid stealing text-entry keys and can be disabled or remapped.

items.title: Use one interface accent consistently across splash and app
items.acceptance: Primary actions and progress use the approved light/dark accent roles; no decorative rainbow accent remains.

items.title: Describe indexing progress with current and total counts
items.acceptance: Progress wording reports meaningful counts and stage, handles unknown totals, and resolves when work ends.

items.title: Replace the always-green drop zone with a quiet drag-active treatment
items.acceptance: Neutral idle state does not compete with the image; drag-over state is obvious and accessible.

items.title: Place the histogram near the top of the adjustment panel
items.acceptance: Histogram is quickly discoverable and does not crowd the most-used controls at narrow panel widths.

items.title: Make the canvas surround neutral and adjustable
items.acceptance: Canvas surroundings avoid colour casts and offer a restrained user adjustment without obscuring image edges.

items.title: Treat the dark image canvas as an intentional constant in light mode
items.acceptance: Light-mode panels remain light while the image viewing area is a deliberate neutral dark surround.

items.title: Fix filmstrip thumbnail proportions and current-photo emphasis
items.acceptance: Thumbnails preserve image ratio, selected photo is unmistakable and no black stretch tiles appear.

items.title: Show which panels and tools contain edits
items.acceptance: Edited state is indicated without colour alone; double-click reset targets the intended value or section.

items.title: Make before/after comparison prominent and easy to hold
items.acceptance: Press-and-hold reveals original and release restores edited view; comparison remains obvious and keyboard accessible.

items.title: Give colour sliders meaningful tracks and precise value entry
items.acceptance: Track preview reflects the parameter, exact values can be entered, and keyboard/screen-reader operation remains intact.

items.title: Preview each film look on the current photo
items.acceptance: Thumbnails reflect the current source photo and look, update safely after photo changes, and avoid blocking editing.

items.title: Present looks as a film-frame strip with current-image previews
items.acceptance: Look choices read as an intentional photographic collection, show legible names and preserve search/filter access.

items.title: Make slider tracks preview the effect being adjusted
items.acceptance: Temperature, hue, exposure and grain tracks communicate direction/intensity and retain clear focus states.

items.title: Add a before/after wipe with a centred snap point
items.acceptance: Divider drag compares aligned images, snaps at centre and has a hold-to-original shortcut.

items.title: Define shared motion durations and easing for the interface
items.acceptance: A small motion token set covers common transitions and has a verified reduced-motion fallback.

items.title: Apply one purposeful motion language across app surfaces
items.acceptance: Library and Editor share transition principles; system reduced-motion preference is respected everywhere.

items.title: Unify interface typography and reserve expressive type for the brand
items.acceptance: Interface uses the existing typography system consistently; numeric values align; any font change requires a real linked font and context rationale.

items.title: Add an anti-generic visual rule set to design review and checks
items.acceptance: Rules encode approved palette, hierarchy, states and image-first principles; checks catch objective violations without banning purposeful exceptions.

items.title: Add a neutral colour-assessment viewing mode
items.acceptance: Toggle shows a controlled mid-grey and white border for judgement and restores the prior canvas view.

items.title: Add shadow and highlight clipping indicators tied to the histogram
items.acceptance: Clipping warnings can be toggled, are visible on the photo, and have keyboard and accessible labels.

items.title: Preview output profiles with soft proofing
items.acceptance: Named output profiles and rendering intent are visible; proof mode is clearly indicated and does not overwrite the edit.

items.title: Add a pinned reference image beside the active edit
items.acceptance: Reference persists while editing, supports side-by-side orientations and can be replaced from Library context.

items.title: Search adjustment controls by name and concept
items.acceptance: Search finds controls across panels, focuses the result and preserves a clear route back to its section.

items.title: Separate reset value, reset section and revert-photo actions
items.acceptance: Each reset action states its scope; whole-photo revert is protected when edits exist and is undoable where possible.

items.title: Support named virtual versions of one photo edit
items.acceptance: Users can branch, name, compare and delete edit versions while preserving the original source.

items.title: Make copied edits selectively applicable by category
items.acceptance: Copy/paste presents explicit edit categories and handles unsupported/local-only adjustments clearly.

items.title: Present AI edit results as reviewable alternatives
items.acceptance: AI output does not silently replace current work; candidate, keep, refine and discard states are clear.

items.title: Communicate AI mask uncertainty and provide direct correction
items.acceptance: Uncertain mask edges can be identified without colour-only cues and corrected with existing manual tools.

items.title: Connect selected controls and mask rows to their canvas region
items.acceptance: Focusing a mask/sample/crop control highlights the corresponding canvas region without hiding the image.

items.title: Show units beside every technical adjustment value
items.acceptance: Values include correct units or symbols and accessible names include the same context.

items.title: Build a deliberate duplicate-review and merge surface
items.acceptance: Candidate pairs are comparable, metadata explains the match, and merge/delete consequences are explicit and recoverable.

items.title: Offer compact and comfortable interaction-density settings
items.acceptance: Density setting applies consistently, persists, and maintains usable targets and supported resize states.

items.title: Audit high-contrast and forced-colour states across controls
items.acceptance: Selection, focus, mask and slider states remain identifiable without colour alone in high-contrast settings.

items.title: Turn the token report into a visual quality and coverage dashboard
items.acceptance: Opening summary includes contrast, component-state coverage, visual changes, unused/dynamic icons and theme/viewport gaps.

items.title: Use quiet, consistent RAW and video badges
items.acceptance: Media type is discoverable without a persistent loud badge on every tile.

items.title: Replace the Library logo badge with a compact monochrome mark
items.acceptance: The brand mark fits the Library header and uses the established palette without an unrelated orange badge.

items.title: Soften sidebar dividers and use spacing for grouping
items.acceptance: Sidebar sections remain easy to distinguish with fewer heavy separators.

items.title: Reveal rating, flag and applied look on thumbnail hover
items.acceptance: Useful metadata appears on hover/focus without permanently covering important image content.

items.title: Scale grid spacing with thumbnail size
items.acceptance: Zoom levels use intentional gaps from compact to spacious and preserve a stable grid rhythm.

items.title: Add an on-demand photo information panel
items.acceptance: A keyboard-accessible toggle reveals metadata for the selected photo and preserves the grid context.

items.title: Navigate library time ranges with continuous zoom levels
items.acceptance: Users can move between year/month/day groupings with pointer and keyboard, with clear current context.

items.title: Add Survey view for comparing selected photos
items.acceptance: Two to eight chosen photos fit the view; removing one preserves the rest and selection is keyboard operable.

items.title: Add colour-based photo filtering
items.acceptance: A user can choose a hue range and receive understandable, repeatable results with an accessible alternative to colour alone.

items.title: Group photos by applied film look
items.acceptance: Group headers identify the applied look and photos remain reachable in their original collection.

items.title: Add a timeline scrubber for large libraries
items.acceptance: Dragging to a date shows a clear month/year preview and navigates to the matching photos.

items.title: Pin a small highlights row above All Photos
items.acceptance: Recent edits, favourites and pinned collections are useful, dismissible and do not displace the photo grid excessively.

items.title: Add back and forward history for Library navigation
items.acceptance: Back/forward restores collection and photo context, including scroll position where practical.

items.title: Add an optional focus mode for the canvas and grid
items.acceptance: Panels can be temporarily tucked away and restored explicitly; no surprise edge-triggered overlays; reduced motion is respected.

items.title: Save named workspaces for different editing tasks
items.acceptance: Workspace layout can be saved, restored, renamed and reset without changing photo edits.

items.title: Use one filmstrip for Library neighbours and Editor look previews
items.acceptance: The strip has clear mode labels and selection semantics in both contexts; switching modes does not lose place.

items.title: Make the splash photograph fill the opening card
items.acceptance: Photo leads the composition while logo and progress remain legible across supported sizes.

items.title: Remove stacked glow effects from the wordmark
items.acceptance: Wordmark is crisp and readable against varied photo tones without multiple glow shadows.

items.title: Align splash corner treatment with the product surfaces
items.acceptance: Splash and app corners feel intentionally related without flattening the photo's own crop.

items.title: Group the tool rail into Look, Fix and Output tasks
items.acceptance: All tools remain reachable and labels/grouping survive compact and expanded rail states.

items.title: Add camera-like value scrubbing with detents and fine adjustment
items.acceptance: Horizontal drag adjusts value, common neutral points are reachable, and modifier fine-tuning is discoverable.

items.title: Connect tonal controls to relevant histogram regions
items.acceptance: Hover/focus highlights the affected tonal region; live updates communicate the relationship without blocking edits.

items.title: Show edit history as a scrub-able visual strip
items.acceptance: History snapshots can be inspected and restored; current state and original are clearly identified.

items.title: Use measured labels and tabular numerals for adjustment values
items.acceptance: Section labels remain readable and value width does not jitter as numbers change; no new font without a linked, context-tested proposal.

items.title: Make panel and menu motion interruptible
items.acceptance: Reversing an in-flight transition continues naturally from its current position without state desynchronization.

items.title: Ease slider value jumps without trailing direct manipulation
items.acceptance: Track input follows the pointer directly; typed or stepped changes use brief easing and reduced motion removes it.

items.title: Animate panel disclosure with a reduced-motion alternative
items.acceptance: Section height, content and disclosure icon move as one; reduced motion uses an immediate or short fade state.

items.title: Show monitor and destination gamut warnings
items.acceptance: Two warning types are distinguishable, explained, configurable and removable from the preview.

items.title: Support a clean secondary-display viewer
items.acceptance: A second display can show a clean image/reference while controls remain on the primary display; disconnect is safe.

items.title: Add a temporary Solo mode for adjustment-panel sections
items.acceptance: A documented modifier/gesture isolates one section and restores siblings without losing their open state.

items.title: Show provenance for user, preset, pasted and AI-generated changes
items.acceptance: History entries identify source and allow inspection before accepting any AI-produced edit.

items.title: Explain local processing where AI features are introduced
items.acceptance: A concise, accurate privacy explanation appears at first meaningful use and does not overclaim data handling.

items.title: Give the tone curve enough space for precise manipulation
items.acceptance: Curve is large enough for nodes, channel identity stays visible, and resizing does not clip controls.

items.title: Pin multiple colour samples to the photo for live readout
items.acceptance: Samples persist while adjusting and show the selected readout space and values with a remove action.

items.title: Add optional slider detents at meaningful values
items.acceptance: Common values are easy to land on without preventing continuous fine adjustment.

items.title: Make fine adjustment mode visible while it is active
items.acceptance: Modifier state is visible and temporary; tick marks and value scale communicate increased precision.

items.title: Use temporary on-canvas tool hints on first use
items.acceptance: Hints point to the relevant interaction, disappear after use and do not obstruct keyboard or screen-reader flows.

items.title: Let the gallery scroll beneath a restrained floating toolbar
items.acceptance: Toolbar stays legible over scrolling content, respects reduced transparency, and does not obscure photos or controls.

items.title: Offer a masonry gallery as an alternate view
items.acceptance: Masonry is an explicit optional layout; ordering, selection and scrolling remain coherent.

items.title: Transition a thumbnail into the Editor canvas
items.acceptance: Transition tracks the source tile when available, falls back safely when not, preserves state and supports reduced motion.

items.title: Carry the splash photo into its Library tile
items.acceptance: Handoff occurs only when the tile is known and visible; otherwise use a brief graceful crossfade.

items.title: Rotate a small set of recent user edits as splash artwork
items.acceptance: Only local, available images are used; labels identify looks accurately; private or missing assets fall back safely.

items.title: Fade the splash into the Library without an empty flash
items.acceptance: Transition has no blank frame, is brief and obeys reduced-motion settings.

items.title: Use subtle film texture only on selected non-photo surfaces
items.acceptance: Texture is static/subtle, never overlays the user image, and preserves text contrast and reduced-motion behaviour.

items.title: Fade thumbnails in once without replaying on scroll
items.acceptance: Initial image arrival is subtle and brief, reused tiles do not replay, and rapid navigation is not delayed.

items.title: Add clear but stable hover and selection feedback to gallery tiles
items.acceptance: Hover/focus/selection states are distinct and do not shift neighbouring tiles or disrupt dense-grid scanning.

items.title: Prototype an optional radial menu for frequent Editor actions
items.acceptance: Prototype is discoverable, keyboard accessible, does not replace context menus and passes usability review before adoption.

items.title: Restore a visible hover affordance on Library topbar icon buttons
items.acceptance: Library topbar icon buttons have a visible hover treatment consistent with the design tokens and the current interaction state.
items.note: Linked follow-up created while committing backlog item 4: the pre-existing wireframe inventory reports the Library topbar icon button hover background does not change, while the wireframe expects a visible lift. Kept out of item 4 scope.

id_policy: id is the new priority-ordered sequence; source_id preserves the original recommendation number from 1-100.
